title: Add Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) driver support — Phase 1
description:
## Summary

Add first-phase support for Kubernetes Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA,
KEP-4381 structured parameters) alongside the existing classic Device Plugin
API framework. This is exploratory, post-POC scope (the classic Device
Plugin API POC takes priority) — Phase 1 is deliberately thin: enough to
demonstrate structured-parameter allocation end-to-end on a single node,
without the production-hardening (multi-slice splitting, health streaming,
v1beta1 compatibility) that later phases will add.

Full design and rationale: `docs/dra-design.md` (branch `dra-support`).

## Scope (Phase 1)

- New `core` types/traits for DRA-facing pool discovery and claim
  preparation.
- New `dra` cargo feature in `proto` compiling `dra/v1/api.proto` and
  `pluginregistration/v1/api.proto`.
- New `dra` workspace crate: pluginwatcher-based registration server,
  `DRAPlugin` gRPC service (`NodePrepareResources`/`NodeUnprepareResources`),
  a `ResourceClaim` resolver, a single-slice `ResourceSlice` publisher, and
  the lifecycle harness wiring them together.
- Minimal RBAC + DaemonSet manifests sufficient to validate against a real
  (or kind) cluster, with `maxSurge: 0` (kubelet does not support rolling
  updates of node plugins pre-1.33).
- Test harness mirroring the existing `test` crate's mock kubelet helpers,
  adapted for the inverted (plugin-as-server) registration model.
- End-to-end validation against a real cluster.

## Explicit non-goals for Phase 1

- `v1beta1` DRA API compatibility (targeting `v1` only).
- Multi-slice `ResourceSlice` pooling/splitting for driver device counts
  above the ~128-device-per-slice limit.
- `DRAResourceHealth` streaming.
- A deployable example crate mirroring `example/`.

These are tracked as future phases in `docs/dra-design.md`, not rejected —
they'll get their own epics once Phase 1 ships.

## Success Criteria

- A `dra` crate exists in the workspace, builds, and passes its own test
  suite in CI alongside the existing crates.
- A minimal DRA driver built on this crate: registers with kubelet via the
  plugin-watcher mechanism, publishes a single `ResourceSlice` describing
  its devices, and successfully prepares/unprepares a `ResourceClaim` for a
  real pod on a real (or kind) cluster running a `v1`-capable kubelet.
- The driver survives a restart without leaving kubelet or the API server in
  an inconsistent state (idempotent `NodePrepareResources`, clean
  re-registration).
- `docs/dra-design.md` is updated with any findings from implementation that
  contradict or refine the design (see its "Open risks" section).

title: DRA: add core types and traits for resource-pool discovery and claim preparation
description:
## Summary

Add the DRA-facing abstractions to the `core` crate, mirroring the existing
`DeviceDiscovery`/`DeviceAllocator`/`K8sDevicePlugin` pattern (see
`core/src/lib.rs`, `core/src/device.rs`) but shaped for DRA's claim-based
model instead of the classic plugin's device-ID-list model. These are pure
data/trait definitions: no gRPC, no Kubernetes API client, no async runtime
specifics beyond `async_trait` — matching `core`'s existing
zero-network-dependency design.

Full rationale: `docs/dra-design.md`, "`core` additions" section.

## Details

Add the following to `core` (new module, e.g. `core/src/dra.rs`, exported
from `core/src/lib.rs`):

- `AttributeValue` — enum covering the attribute value kinds DRA's
  CEL-based selectors match against: `String(String)`, `Int(i64)`,
  `Bool(bool)`, `Version(String)` (semver-ish version string per the DRA
  API).
- `Quantity` — a resource quantity type for device capacity (can wrap a
  simple numeric representation initially; revisit if `k8s-openapi`'s
  `Quantity` type is more appropriate once the `dra` crate's Kubernetes
  client dependency is in place).
- `PoolDevice` — `{ name: String, attributes: HashMap<String,
  AttributeValue>, capacity: HashMap<String, Quantity>, health: Health }`.
  Reuses the existing `core::Health` enum.
- `ResourcePool` trait — `async fn devices(&self) -> HashMap<String,
  Vec<PoolDevice>>` (keyed by pool name). The DRA analog of
  `DeviceDiscovery`.
- `ClaimRef` — `{ namespace: String, uid: String, name: String }`, matching
  the wire-level `dra.v1.Claim` message fields exactly.
- `AllocatedDevice` — `{ pool_name: String, device_name: String,
  request_name: Option<String> }`, matching what a resolved
  `ResourceClaim.status.allocation` entry looks like.
- `ResolvedClaim` — `{ claim: ClaimRef, devices: Vec<AllocatedDevice> }`.
- `PreparedDevice` — the DRA analog of `ContainerAllocation`: at minimum
  `cdi_device_ids: Vec<String>`, `request_names: Vec<String>` (mirrors
  `dra.v1.Device`'s fields so the `dra` crate's proto-mapping layer is a
  direct field-for-field translation).
- `PrepareError` — `thiserror`-based enum analogous to `AllocationError`
  (e.g. `ClaimNotAllocated`, `DeviceUnavailable(String)`,
  `HookFailed(String)`), matching the existing project convention of
  `thiserror` for all core error types.
- `ClaimPreparer` trait:

  ```rust
  #[async_trait]
  pub trait ClaimPreparer: Send + Sync {
      async fn prepare(
          &self,
          claims: &[ResolvedClaim],
      ) -> HashMap<ClaimRef, Result<Vec<PreparedDevice>, PrepareError>>;
      async fn unprepare(&self, claim: &ClaimRef) -> Result<(), PrepareError>;
  }
  ```

  Note the batch signature (`&[ResolvedClaim]` in, one result per claim
  out) — this matches both the wire-level `NodePrepareResourcesRequest`'s
  `repeated Claim claims` shape and upstream's
  `k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/kubeletplugin` helper's
  `PrepareResourceClaims(claims)` signature. Do **not** make this
  one-claim-per-call; see `docs/dra-design.md` for why.

  Document on the trait that implementations **must** be idempotent —
  kubelet may call `prepare` again for an already-prepared claim (e.g.
  after the driver restarts), and must return the same result rather than
  erroring or double-provisioning.
- `DraDriver` trait — `pub trait DraDriver: ResourcePool + ClaimPreparer {
  fn driver_name(&self) -> &str; }`, the DRA analog of `K8sDevicePlugin`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All types/traits above exist in `core`, exported from
      `core/src/lib.rs`, with the same doc-comment density/style as the
      existing `DeviceDiscovery`/`DeviceAllocator` traits.
- [ ] `PrepareError` uses `thiserror::Error` and implements `Clone + Debug +
      PartialEq + Eq` like `AllocationError` does today.
- [ ] Unit tests exercise a trivial static `DraDriver` implementation
      analogous to the existing `StaticPlugin` test fixture in
      `core/src/lib.rs`'s test module — at minimum: `devices()` returns the
      expected pool map, `prepare()` on a batch of 2+ claims returns
      per-claim results keyed correctly, `unprepare()` on an unknown claim
      doesn't panic.
- [ ] No new dependencies added to `core/Cargo.toml` beyond what it already
      has (`async-trait`, `thiserror`) — this crate must stay free of
      gRPC/Kubernetes-client dependencies per the design's crate-boundary
      goal.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace` and `cargo test -p k8s-device-plugin-core`
      pass.
close_reason: done

title: DRA: minimal RBAC and DaemonSet manifests for cluster validation
description:
## Summary

Produce the minimal Kubernetes manifests needed to run a Phase-1 DRA driver
built on the `dra` crate against a real (or kind) cluster for the
end-to-end validation task — not a full polished deployable example crate
(that's Phase 4 per `docs/dra-design.md`), just enough YAML to prove the
design works.

## Details

- `ServiceAccount` + `ClusterRole`/`ClusterRoleBinding` (or `Role`/
  `RoleBinding` if scoping allows) granting: read (`get`/`list`/`watch`) on
  `resourceclaims.resource.k8s.io`, and create/update/patch/delete on
  `resourceslices.resource.k8s.io`, plus read on `nodes` (needed for the
  owner-reference lookup in the publisher task). Per `docs/dra-design.md`'s
  open-risk note, look at
  [`dra-example-driver`'s Helm templates](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-example-driver/tree/main/deployments/helm/dra-example-driver/templates)
  for the recommended Validating Admission Policy pattern that scopes
  `ResourceClaim`/`ResourceSlice` access to the local node, and adopt it if
  it's not disproportionate effort for a validation-only manifest set (use
  judgment — a plain, slightly-too-broad `ClusterRole` is acceptable for
  Phase 1 validation if the VAP is a lot of additional YAML for a manifest
  set that won't ship to the customer; note the gap explicitly if so).
- `DaemonSet` running the Phase 1 driver binary, with **`maxSurge: 0`**
  explicitly set (verify whether this is already the k8s default for
  `RollingUpdate` DaemonSets and set it explicitly anyway so the constraint
  is self-documenting rather than relying on an implicit default), mounting
  `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins_registry/` and
  `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/<driver-name>/` as `hostPath` volumes (matching
  how `example/k8s/`'s existing DaemonSet mounts
  `/var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/` for the classic plugin — check that
  manifest for the exact volume-mount/security-context conventions already
  established), and the `NODE_NAME` downward-API env var the publisher
  task's owner-reference lookup needs.
- Since there's no real driver binary yet (Phase 1's tasks build the
  *library*, not a shipped binary), this task's manifests should target a
  minimal throwaway test binary (e.g. `dra/examples/minimal_driver.rs`,
  analogous to `lib/examples/example_plugin.rs`) built for this validation
  purpose — this belongs in this task since the manifests are meaningless
  without something to deploy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Manifests apply cleanly to a real or kind cluster with DRA
      structured parameters enabled (`resource.k8s.io/v1` available).
- [ ] The DaemonSet pod starts, and the RBAC grants are sufficient for it
      to reach the API server (no RBAC-denial errors in pod logs).
- [ ] `maxSurge: 0` is explicit in the manifest, with a comment citing
      `docs/dra-design.md`'s deployment note.
- [ ] A minimal example driver binary exists to deploy (doesn't need real
      hardware backing — a fake/static device list, matching how
      `StaticDevicePlugin` serves this role for the classic plugin's
      quickstart, is fine and arguably preferable for repeatable
      validation).

title: DRA: end-to-end validation against a real cluster
description:
## Summary

Prove Phase 1 actually works by running the minimal driver from the
RBAC/manifests task against a real (or kind, if kind supports the required
DRA feature gates/API — verify at implementation time; DRA structured
parameters may require a specific kind node image or `--feature-gates`
config) cluster, exercising the full path from `DeviceClass`/`ResourceClaim`
creation through pod scheduling to `NodePrepareResources`.

## Details

Manual or scripted (prefer scripted and checked into the repo, e.g.
`dra/hack/e2e-smoke.sh`, if it can be made reasonably reliable — but don't
over-invest in full CI automation for this validation-only task; a
documented manual runbook is an acceptable fallback) walkthrough covering:

1. Cluster has DRA structured parameters enabled and `resource.k8s.io/v1`
   available (record the exact k8s version/feature-gate config used, since
   this becomes the minimum supported version for Phase 1 — update
   `docs/dra-design.md`'s "target: v1 only" note with the concrete version
   once confirmed).
2. Deploy the RBAC + DaemonSet from the previous task; confirm via
   `kubectl get pods` and driver logs that registration succeeded
   (kubelet's plugin-watcher picked it up — confirm via kubelet logs too,
   not just the driver's own claim of success, since a driver can believe
   it registered while kubelet silently rejected it).
3. Confirm exactly one `ResourceSlice` appears (`kubectl get
   resourceslices`) with the expected `driver`/`pool`/`devices` fields.
4. Create a `DeviceClass` selecting this driver's devices, a
   `ResourceClaim` (or `ResourceClaimTemplate` via a pod) requesting one,
   and a pod referencing it.
5. Confirm the pod schedules, the driver's `NodePrepareResources` gets
   called (via driver logs/tracing spans) with the correct claim
   reference, and the pod starts successfully with the expected CDI device
   visible inside the container.
6. Delete the pod; confirm `NodeUnprepareResources` is called and cleans
   up.
7. **Idempotency check** (this is the important one the design doc flags
   as an open risk): kill and restart the driver pod while a prepared
   claim is still in use by a running pod; confirm the driver comes back
   up, re-registers, and — if kubelet calls `NodePrepareResources` again
   for the still-in-use claim — returns the same result without erroring
   or double-provisioning. Record what kubelet actually does here (call
   again? not call again? something else?) since this answers one of
   `docs/dra-design.md`'s explicitly open risks.
8. Confirm the `maxSurge: 0` / no-rolling-update behavior matches what
   `docs/dra-design.md`'s deployment note predicts (old pod fully
   terminates, brief gap, new pod starts) rather than assuming it without
   observing it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All 8 steps above pass, with the concrete k8s version and any
      non-default feature gates used recorded in `docs/dra-design.md`
      (replacing its currently-hypothetical "target: v1 only" framing with
      a confirmed minimum version).
- [ ] The restart/idempotency finding from step 7 is written back into
      `docs/dra-design.md`'s "Open risks" section as a resolved item (or,
      if it turns up a real bug, a new bug ticket is filed against the
      DRAPlugin-service or lifecycle-harness task's implementation rather
      than silently working around it in the validation script).
- [ ] Whatever validation script/runbook is produced is checked into the
      repo (`dra/hack/` or `dra/README.md`) so this isn't a one-off,
      unrepeatable manual exercise for the next person touching this code.

title: DRA: scaffold new dra workspace crate
description:
## Summary

Create the new `dra` workspace crate that will host the DRA runtime
(registration server, `DRAPlugin` gRPC service, `ResourceSlice` publisher,
lifecycle harness). This is scaffolding only — no functional
gRPC/Kubernetes-client code — so the remaining Phase 1 tasks (registration
server, claim resolver, plugin service, slice publisher, lifecycle harness)
have a crate to land in and can proceed in parallel once this merges.

## Details

- Add `dra/Cargo.toml` as a new workspace member (update root
  `Cargo.toml`'s `[workspace] members` list, matching the pattern of
  `core`/`lib`/`proto`/`test`/`example`).
- Package name: `k8s-device-plugin-dra` (matching the existing
  `k8s-device-plugin-{core,lib,proto,test}` naming convention),
  version/edition/repository inherited from `[workspace.package]` like the
  other crates.
- Dependencies: `k8s-device-plugin-core` (path dep), `k8s-device-plugin-proto`
  (path dep, with its `dra` feature enabled — depends on the
  proto-compilation task), `tonic`, `tokio`, `async-trait`, `thiserror`,
  `tracing` (all already in `[workspace.dependencies]`, reuse those version
  pins rather than introducing new ones — project convention: pin to at
  least MAJOR.MINOR, never a bare major).
- New dependencies this crate specifically needs, to be added to
  `[workspace.dependencies]` with explicit MAJOR.MINOR pins: `kube` (with
  the `client`, `runtime`, `derive` features as needed) and `k8s-openapi`
  (with a features flag matching the target Kubernetes minor version — pick
  the feature matching whatever cluster version Phase 1 validation targets;
  confirm against the cluster used in the end-to-end validation task before
  pinning). Research current stable versions of both crates at
  implementation time rather than guessing here.
- `dra/src/lib.rs` — empty module skeleton with a doc-comment header
  explaining the crate's role (mirroring `lib/src/lib.rs`'s module-level
  doc comment style), plus placeholder `mod` declarations for the modules
  the subsequent tasks will fill in (`registration`, `service`,
  `resourceslice`, `claim`) so those tasks don't also need to touch
  `lib.rs`'s module wiring.
- Add the new crate to CI (GitHub Actions workflow) alongside the existing
  crates — check whatever workflow file currently runs `cargo
  test`/`cargo clippy` across the workspace; if it already runs
  `--workspace`, no change needed beyond registering the crate as a
  workspace member, but verify this explicitly rather than assuming.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: DRA: compile dra/v1 and pluginregistration/v1 protos behind a dra feature
description:
## Summary

Extend the `proto` crate to compile the two `.proto` files Phase 1 actually
needs — `kubelet/pkg/apis/dra/v1/api.proto` and
`kubelet/pkg/apis/pluginregistration/v1/api.proto` — behind a new `dra`
Cargo feature, so classic device-plugin consumers (`lib`, `example`) don't
pay for or pull in generated DRA code they don't use.

## Details

- `proto/Cargo.toml`: add a `dra = []` feature.
- `proto/build.rs`: currently unconditionally compiles only
  `deviceplugin/v1beta1/api.proto` via a single
  `tonic_prost_build::configure().compile_protos(&[...], &[])` call. Extend
  this so that when the `dra` feature is enabled (check via
  `std::env::var("CARGO_FEATURE_DRA").is_ok()` in `build.rs` — feature
  flags aren't visible to `cfg!`/`#[cfg]` inside the build script itself,
  only via the `CARGO_FEATURE_<NAME>` env var Cargo sets), it additionally
  compiles `kubelet/pkg/apis/dra/v1/api.proto` and
  `kubelet/pkg/apis/pluginregistration/v1/api.proto`. The two DRA protos
  are in different packages (`k8s.io.kubelet.pkg.apis.dra.v1` vs
  `pluginregistration`) — compile them together in one
  `compile_protos(&[both paths], &[])` call so cross-references resolve,
  matching how `tonic_prost_build` handles multi-file compilation
  elsewhere; verify at implementation time whether a single call or two
  separate calls is actually required/supported.
- `proto/src/lib.rs`: add a `dra` module (gated `#[cfg(feature = "dra")]`)
  analogous to the existing `pub mod v1beta1 { ...
  tonic::include_proto!("v1beta1"); }` block. Expose the generated
  `DRAPlugin` client/server traits, the `Registration` client/server traits
  from `pluginregistration.v1` (note: this is a **second**, distinct
  `Registration` service definition from the one already compiled for
  `deviceplugin/v1beta1` — the two are structurally similar but are
  different generated Rust types since they come from different `.proto`
  packages; do not attempt to unify them), plus relevant constants (kubelet
  plugin/registry directory paths: `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/` and
  `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins_registry/`, mirroring how
  `v1beta1::DEVICE_PLUGIN_PATH` is defined today).
- Confirm the `pluginregistration` package's odd `package pluginregistration;
  // This should have been v1.` comment (see the vendored proto file)
  doesn't cause a Rust module naming collision with the `deviceplugin`
  proto's registration types once both are compiled into the same crate —
  `tonic::include_proto!` keys off the proto `package` name, and both
  `deviceplugin/v1beta1/api.proto`'s embedded `Registration` service and
  `pluginregistration/v1/api.proto`'s `Registration` service could
  plausibly generate colliding module paths; verify and disambiguate
  before this is considered done.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `cargo build -p k8s-device-plugin-proto` (default, no `dra` feature)
      behaves identically to today — no new generated code, no new
      build-time proto compilation.
- [ ] `cargo build -p k8s-device-plugin-proto --features dra` compiles both
      new protos successfully and exposes them from a `dra` module in
      `proto/src/lib.rs`.
- [ ] No naming collision between the pre-existing `v1beta1::Registration*`
      types and the new `dra::Registration*` types when both are compiled
      into the same crate (i.e. `--all-features` builds cleanly).
- [ ] `cargo clippy -p k8s-device-plugin-proto --features dra` passes with
      the workspace's lint configuration (see root `Cargo.toml`'s
      `[workspace.lints]`).

title: DRA: implement pluginwatcher-based Registration server
description:
## Summary

Implement `DraRegistrationServer` in the `dra` crate: the plugin-side gRPC
**server** for kubelet's generic plugin-watcher mechanism
(`pluginregistration.v1.Registration`). This is the inverted counterpart of
the existing `RegistrationClient` in `lib/src/registration.rs` — for DRA,
the plugin serves `GetInfo`/`NotifyRegistrationStatus` and kubelet connects
to it, rather than the plugin calling kubelet.

## Details

Reference: `docs/dra-design.md`'s "`dra` crate runtime components" section
and the linked upstream `noderegistrar.go`/`registrationserver.go` in
`k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/kubeletplugin`.

- Listens on a Unix socket at
  `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins_registry/<driver-name>-reg.sock`. Reuse `lib`'s
  `sanitize_socket_name`/`fnv1a64` truncate-plus-hash scheme (currently
  private to `lib/src/lib.rs`) rather than re-deriving it — either move it
  to a small shared location both crates can use, or duplicate the ~15-line
  function with a comment pointing at the original if sharing isn't worth a
  new dependency edge between `lib` and `dra` (these two crates should
  otherwise remain independent per the design's crate-boundary goal — use
  judgment here, but don't silently let the two implementations drift, e.g.
  keep both under test with the same edge-case unit tests `lib` already
  has: `sanitize_socket_name_is_deterministic`,
  `sanitize_socket_name_does_not_collide_across_distinct_names`,
  `sanitize_socket_name_keeps_full_endpoint_within_socket_path_limit`).
- Implements `GetInfo` — returns `PluginInfo { type: "DRAPlugin", name:
  <driver-name>, endpoint: <path to the DRAPlugin service socket, see the
  plugin-service task>, supported_versions: vec!["v1"] }` per the Phase 1
  non-goal of `v1`-only support.
- Implements `NotifyRegistrationStatus` — logs the outcome via `tracing`
  (matching the project's "structured tracing events and spans, never raw
  println" convention documented in root `README.md`'s Observability
  section); on `plugin_registered: false`, log at `tracing::error!` with
  the `error` field from the request.
- Socket lifecycle: remove any stale socket file at the target path before
  binding (mirrors `DevicePlugin::setup_listener` in `lib/src/lib.rs`), and
  clean up on shutdown.
- This task does **not** need to implement retry/reconnect logic for
  kubelet restarts — unlike the classic device-plugin flow (where the
  plugin actively re-registers), the plugin-watcher model has kubelet
  re-scanning `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins_registry/` and re-connecting on its
  own; the plugin's job is just to keep the socket alive and correctly
  answer `GetInfo` whenever asked. Document this asymmetry inline where it
  might surprise a reader coming from the classic-plugin codebase.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `DraRegistrationServer` binds its socket, answers `GetInfo` with the
      fields above, and answers `NotifyRegistrationStatus` without
      erroring, verified by a unit test using
      `k8s_device_plugin_test::dra_registration::MockRegistrationClient`
      connected over the Unix socket (mirroring `lib`'s existing
      `registration_client_connects_over_unix_socket` test style).
- [ ] Socket-name sanitization is covered by the same edge-case tests
      `lib` already has for the classic plugin (deterministic,
      non-colliding, path-length-safe).
- [ ] `NotifyRegistrationStatus` failure is logged via `tracing::error!`,
      not silently dropped — verified by a test asserting on a tracing
      subscriber capture, or at minimum manually verified and noted in the
      PR description if a tracing-capture test is impractical here.
- [ ] No blocking I/O on the async runtime (matches the rest of the
      codebase's all-async-Tokio style).
close_reason: DraRegistrationServer implemented in dra/src/registration.rs, serving GetInfo/NotifyRegistrationStatus on a plugins_registry socket. Moved sanitize_socket_name/fnv1a64 to core::socket_name (generalized, budget-parameterized) so lib and dra share it without a new dependency edge. Tests cover get_info, notify success, and notify-failure error logging (custom tracing capture layer). Commit dd6d4ec.

title: DRA: implement ResourceClaim resolver (claim reference -> ResolvedClaim)
description:
## Summary

Implement the component that turns a wire-level `dra.v1.Claim { namespace,
uid, name }` reference (all `NodePrepareResources` gives the driver) into a
`core::ResolvedClaim` by reading the actual `ResourceClaim` object's
`status.allocation.devices` from the Kubernetes API server. This is the
piece that makes the scheduler's allocation decision visible to the driver.

## Details

Reference: `docs/dra-design.md`'s table row "Allocation decision" and the
"`dra` crate runtime components" section.

- Add a `kube::Api<ResourceClaim>` (from `k8s-openapi`'s
  `resource.k8s.io/v1` `ResourceClaim` type, or a hand-written minimal
  struct deriving `kube::Resource` if `k8s-openapi` doesn't cover the
  `resource.k8s.io` API group for the target k8s version — verify at
  implementation time which crate provides these Rust types) scoped
  appropriately — read `docs/dra-design.md`'s open-risk note recommending
  scoping via a Validating Admission Policy to the local node, matching
  `dra-example-driver`'s Helm templates.
- Given a `ClaimRef`, fetch the `ResourceClaim`, verify its `metadata.uid`
  matches the `uid` in the reference (defend against a stale/reused
  name+namespace pointing at a different object — the UID is the
  authoritative identity per the wire protocol's own doc comments), and
  verify `status.allocation` is present (if absent, the claim isn't
  actually allocated yet — this shouldn't happen if kubelet only calls
  `NodePrepareResources` for allocated claims, but per upstream's own
  defensive-driver guidance, don't assume; return a clear `PrepareError`
  rather than panicking or producing a bogus empty result).
- Map `status.allocation.devices` (each entry: request name, pool name,
  device name) into `Vec<AllocatedDevice>`.
- Consider whether a shared informer/reflector cache (via
  `kube::runtime::reflector` or a `watcher`) is warranted for Phase 1 vs. a
  direct per-call `Api::get`. Given Phase 1's explicit "thin path" scope
  and that `NodePrepareResources` calls are not high-frequency, a direct
  `Api::get` per claim (batched via `futures::future::join_all` across the
  claims in one `NodePrepareResourcesRequest`) is the recommended Phase 1
  choice — an informer/reflector is more machinery than this phase needs
  and can be revisited in Phase 2 if API-server load becomes a concern.
  Document this choice inline as a deliberate simplification, not an
  oversight.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given a `ClaimRef` for a `ResourceClaim` with a populated
      `status.allocation`, the resolver returns a `ResolvedClaim` whose
      `devices` match the claim's allocation exactly.
- [ ] UID mismatch between the reference and the fetched object is
      detected and surfaced as a `PrepareError`, not silently ignored.
- [ ] A `ResourceClaim` found but without `status.allocation` populated
      yields a clear `PrepareError`, not a panic or an empty-but-"successful"
      `ResolvedClaim`.
- [ ] Unit tests use a fake/mock `kube` client (e.g. `kube::Client`
      against a mock API server via `tower-test`, or whichever approach
      the `kube` crate's own test suite recommends at implementation time)
      rather than requiring a real cluster for this task's tests
      specifically (the real-cluster requirement is deferred to the
      end-to-end validation task).
close_reason: ClaimResolver implemented in dra/src/claim.rs using k8s-openapi's native resource.k8s.io/v1::ResourceClaim type (no hand-written struct needed -- kube-core depends on k8s-openapi unconditionally). resolve() verifies UID match and status.allocation presence, both surfaced as PrepareError (added ResolutionFailed variant; reused existing ClaimNotAllocated). resolve_all() batches via futures::future::join_all per the ticket's guidance. Tests mock kube::Client via tower_test::mock::pair (kube's own canonical test pattern) -- no real cluster needed. Commit 2a0c79b.

title: DRA: implement DRAPlugin gRPC service (NodePrepareResources/NodeUnprepareResources)
description:
## Summary

Implement `DraPluginService`, the `dra` crate's adapter between the
wire-level `dra.v1.DRAPlugin` gRPC service and a backend's
`core::ClaimPreparer`/`core::DraDriver` implementation — the DRA analog of
`lib`'s existing `DevicePluginService`.

## Details

Reference: `docs/dra-design.md`'s "`dra` crate runtime components" section,
and the `dra/v1/api.proto` definitions (`NodePrepareResourcesRequest`/
`Response`, `NodeUnprepareResourcesRequest`/`Response`, `Claim`, `Device`).

- `NodePrepareResources(NodePrepareResourcesRequest { claims: Vec<Claim>
  })`:
  1. For each `Claim` in the request, resolve it to a `ResolvedClaim` via
     the resolver from the claim-resolver task (run these resolutions
     concurrently — mirror the existing `allocate` RPC handler's pattern
     in `lib/src/lib.rs` of spawning one task per item and awaiting in
     order, since claim resolution is API-server I/O and independent per
     claim).
  2. Call `ClaimPreparer::prepare(&resolved_claims)` once with the full
     batch (per the batch-signature decision in the core-types task — do
     not call `prepare` once per claim).
  3. Map the returned `HashMap<ClaimRef, Result<Vec<PreparedDevice>,
     PrepareError>>` into `NodePrepareResourcesResponse { claims:
     HashMap<String, NodePrepareResourceResponse> }`, keyed by claim UID
     per the wire protocol (`NodePrepareResourcesResponse.claims` map key
     is documented in the `.proto` as "claim_uid"). A `PrepareError` for a
     given claim becomes a `NodePrepareResourceResponse { error:
     <message>, devices: vec![] }` entry — **not** an RPC-level error,
     since the `.proto` comments are explicit that per-claim failures must
     be reported inside the response, and an RPC-level error causes
     kubelet to ignore the entire response (re-read the `.proto` doc
     comment on `NodePrepareResources` before implementing: "If an error
     is returned, the response is ignored"). This is a meaningfully
     different error-handling contract than the classic `Allocate` RPC
     (`lib`'s `allocate_error_to_status`/`allocation_error_to_status` maps
     errors to `tonic::Status`) — do not copy that pattern here.
  4. It is a protocol violation for the response to omit an entry for any
     claim listed in the request (per the `.proto` comment: "It is an
     error if some claim ... does not get prepared. NodePrepareResources
     will be called again for those that are missing.") — ensure every
     requested claim UID has an entry in the response map even in edge
     cases (e.g. resolver failure for one claim in a larger batch must not
     cause that claim's entry to be dropped; it should get an error entry
     instead).
- `NodeUnprepareResources(NodeUnprepareResourcesRequest { claims:
  Vec<Claim> })`: analogous — call `ClaimPreparer::unprepare` per claim
  (concurrently), map results into `NodeUnprepareResourcesResponse`, same
  "every claim must have an entry" rule.
- Serves on a Unix socket at
  `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/<driver-name>/plugin.sock` (the path advertised
  as `endpoint` by the registration server from the registration-server
  task).
- Wrap both RPC handlers in `#[tracing::instrument]` spans matching the
  existing convention in `lib/src/lib.rs` (every RPC handler there is
  instrumented) so the same "attach any `tracing` subscriber/metrics layer
  for free" story documented in root `README.md`'s Observability section
  extends to DRA.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Per-claim preparation failures are reported inside
      `NodePrepareResourcesResponse.claims[uid].error`, never as a
      `tonic::Status` RPC-level error.
- [ ] Every claim UID present in the request has a corresponding entry in
      the response map, in all tested failure modes (resolver failure,
      `ClaimPreparer` failure, partial batch failure).
- [ ] `NodePrepareResources` is idempotent: calling it twice in a row for
      the same already-prepared claim returns the same successful result
      both times (verified with a test `ClaimPreparer` fixture that tracks
      call counts, matching the idempotency requirement documented on the
      `core::ClaimPreparer` trait).
- [ ] Concurrent claims in one request are resolved/prepared without one
      claim's failure aborting sibling claims' in-flight work — mirrors
      the existing `allocate` RPC's abort-on-failure behavior being
      intentionally *not* replicated here, since the DRA wire protocol
      requires an entry for every claim regardless of sibling failures
      (unlike classic `Allocate`, where a single container's failure fails
      the whole RPC). Call this distinction out explicitly in a code
      comment since it's the opposite behavior from the sibling `lib`
      implementation.
- [ ] `cargo test -p k8s-device-plugin-dra` covers both RPCs' happy path
      and at least one failure-reporting path each, using
      `k8s_device_plugin_test::dra_plugin::MockDraPluginClient`.
close_reason: DraPluginService implemented in dra/src/service.rs: node_prepare_resources/node_unprepare_resources report per-claim failures inside the response (never as tonic::Status, per the .proto's 'response is ignored on error' contract), guarantee an entry per requested claim regardless of sibling failures, and don't abort in-flight work on one claim's failure (opposite of lib's allocate). Extended core::PreparedDevice with required pool_name/device_name wire fields. 6 tests cover success/failure-reporting/idempotency/sibling-independence for both RPCs via a real Unix socket + mocked kube::Client. Commit 6c615cb.

title: DRA: implement single-slice ResourceSlice publisher
description:
## Summary

Implement `ResourceSlicePublisher`: the Phase 1, deliberately non-hardened
component that turns a `core::ResourcePool::devices()` snapshot into a
single `ResourceSlice` API object per node, so the scheduler can see and
allocate this driver's devices. Explicitly **not** the production-grade
reconciler `docs/dra-design.md` describes for Phase 2 (no splitting across
the ~128-device-per-slice limit, no workqueue, no mutation-cache-based
informer-lag handling) — see the design doc's Phase 2 description and the
linked upstream `resourceslice.Controller` for what this deliberately
defers.

## Details

- Uses a `kube::Api<ResourceSlice>` client (same API-group-availability
  caveat as the claim-resolver task applies here — verify `k8s-openapi`
  coverage for `resource.k8s.io` `ResourceSlice` at implementation time).
- On startup and on every change reported by `ResourcePool::devices()`
  (poll on an interval, mirroring `DevicePluginService`'s existing
  `DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL`/`with_poll_interval` pattern in `lib/src/lib.rs`
  — reuse that constant/configurability shape for consistency rather than
  inventing a new knob), compute the desired `ResourceSlice` spec (`driver:
  <driver-name>`, `pool: { name, generation, resourceSliceCount: 1 }`,
  `nodeName: <local node name>`, `devices: [...]` mapped from
  `PoolDevice`) and either create or update the one slice this driver owns
  for this node.
- The slice must be owned by the local `Node` object (an owner reference)
  so it's garbage-collected automatically if the node is deleted — matches
  the design doc's "no GC beyond relying on the Node owner-reference" Phase
  1 scope note. Look up the local `Node` object's UID once at startup (via
  the `NODE_NAME` env var, the standard Downward-API pattern for
  DaemonSets — see the RBAC/manifests task) to construct the owner
  reference.
- Naming: pick a stable, deterministic `ResourceSlice` name (e.g.
  `<node-name>-<driver-name-sanitized>`) or let the API server generate one
  via `generateName` plus a label selector to find "the" slice this driver
  owns on this node when checking whether to create vs. update — decide
  which approach is simpler given `kube-rs`'s API and document the choice.
- Detect drift from a source other than this driver (e.g. someone manually
  edited the slice) only to the extent of "does my last-applied spec still
  match what I read back" — full informer-based drift detection is Phase 2
  scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On startup with N devices reported by `ResourcePool::devices()`,
      exactly one `ResourceSlice` is created on the API server with
      `driver`, `pool.name`, `nodeName`, and `devices` matching.
- [ ] When `ResourcePool::devices()`'s output changes (device
      added/removed/attribute changed), the existing slice is updated in
      place rather than a duplicate slice being created.
- [ ] The slice carries an owner reference to the local `Node`.
- [ ] Tests use a fake/mock `kube` client (same approach as the
      claim-resolver task) — no real cluster required for this task's unit
      tests.
- [ ] The polling interval is configurable via a builder method analogous
      to `DevicePluginService::with_poll_interval`, with the same default
      (or a documented, deliberately different default if devices are
      expected to change less often than health status does — use
      judgment, document the choice).
close_reason: ResourceSlicePublisher implemented in dra/src/resourceslice.rs: one ResourceSlice per pool key from ResourcePool::devices(), created if absent, updated in place (generation bumped) only when devices actually changed, owner-referenced to the local Node. Owns its own poll loop (spawn/with_poll_interval, 30s default). 4 tests via mocked kube::Client caught and fixed a real round-trip-equality bug in the attribute/capacity mapping. Commit 5a56eb4.

title: DRA: implement DraPlugin::run() lifecycle harness
description:
## Summary

Wire the registration server, `DRAPlugin` gRPC service, and `ResourceSlice`
publisher together into a single `DraPlugin` struct with a `run()` method —
the DRA analog of `lib`'s `DevicePlugin::run()` — so a backend author gets
the same "implement one trait, call `.run()`" experience the classic
framework already provides (see root `README.md`'s Quickstart).

## Details

Depends on the registration-server, DRAPlugin-service, and
ResourceSlice-publisher tasks all landing first.

- `DraPlugin::new(driver_name: &str, driver: impl DraDriver + 'static) ->
  Self`, constructing the registration server, the plugin service, and the
  publisher from the one `DraDriver` implementation (which supplies both
  `ResourcePool` and `ClaimPreparer`).
- `run()`: spawn the registration server and the `DRAPlugin` gRPC server as
  concurrent Tokio tasks, spawn the `ResourceSlicePublisher`'s reconcile
  loop as a third concurrent task, and return an error (propagating
  whichever task failed) if any of the three exits unexpectedly — mirror
  `DevicePlugin::run()`'s `tokio::select!`-based structure in
  `lib/src/lib.rs`, adapted for three concurrent components instead of one
  server plus one registration retry loop.
- Unlike the classic `DevicePlugin::run()`, there is no active
  re-registration retry loop to write here (per the registration-server
  task's note that plugin-watcher registration is passive from the
  plugin's side) — but do handle the case where the registration or plugin
  socket needs to be re-created if the underlying file is removed out from
  under the process (e.g. verify behavior if
  `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins_registry/` or
  `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/<driver-name>/` doesn't exist yet at startup —
  these directories may need to be created by the driver, unlike
  `/var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/` which kubelet itself guarantees
  exists).
- Graceful shutdown: on process termination (SIGTERM, matching however the
  classic plugin/example handles shutdown today — check
  `example/src/main.rs` for the existing convention), clean up both
  sockets. Whether to also delete the published `ResourceSlice` on
  graceful shutdown vs. leaving it for the Node-owner-reference GC path is
  a design choice — recommend leaving it (matching the owner-reference GC
  design) rather than adding explicit delete-on-shutdown logic, since a
  competing failure mode (process killed without running shutdown hooks)
  would leave a stale slice either way and the owner-reference path
  already handles the node-deleted case; document this choice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A minimal test `DraDriver` implementation can call
      `DraPlugin::new(...).run()` and have all three components
      (registration server, plugin service, publisher) come up, verified
      against mock/fake backends for the Kubernetes-API-dependent pieces
      (reusing the claim-resolver and publisher tasks' fake-client test
      setups) and a real Unix-socket client for the gRPC-facing pieces
      (reusing `k8s_device_plugin_test::dra_registration::MockRegistrationClient`
      and `MockDraPluginClient`).
- [ ] If any one of the three spawned components fails/panics, `run()`
      returns an error rather than silently continuing with a
      partially-broken plugin.
- [ ] Missing `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins_registry/` or
      `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/<driver-name>/` directories are created if
      absent, with a clear error (not a panic) if creation fails (e.g.
      permissions).
- [ ] Double-check `run()` doesn't assume it's the only instance of the
      driver process running on this *node* at a given instant — fine to
      assume today (Phase 1 has no rolling updates, see

title: Leaked gRPC server task/socket when registration retries are exhausted
description:
run() spawns the DevicePluginServer via tokio::spawn (lib/src/lib.rs:86) and stores the JoinHandle in server_handle. If register_with_retry().await fails after exhausting all attempts (line 90), run() returns Err and server_handle is dropped without being aborted. Dropping a tokio JoinHandle does not cancel the task, so the gRPC server keeps running detached, still bound to the Unix socket at self.endpoint. A supervisor that retries run() after Err leaks one task + one open listener per failed attempt; the next run() only removes the socket *file* (fs::remove_file), not the old listener task, which keeps serving stale RPCs against the original DevicePluginService instance.

Found by high-effort code-review workflow, 2026-07-05.
close_reason: Fixed in 2cbf96e: run() now aborts server_handle before returning Err on registration exhaustion

title: sanitize_socket_name is not injective, allowing socket hijack between distinct resource names
description:
sanitize_socket_name (lib/src/lib.rs:275-277) maps every character that is not alphanumeric/"-"/"_" to "_", and DevicePlugin::new uses its output directly as the Unix socket filename. Two different resource names that differ only in a sanitized character -- e.g. "acme.com/gpu" and "acme_com/gpu" -- both sanitize to "acme_com_gpu". If a second DevicePlugin registers with a colliding sanitized name after the first is already listening, setup_listener() deletes the first plugin's live socket file and binds a new listener at the same path, silently hijacking the first plugin's endpoint; kubelet's subsequent Allocate/ListAndWatch calls for the first resource are served by the wrong plugin (or hang), and the first plugin's listener is orphaned.

Found by high-effort code-review workflow, 2026-07-05.
close_reason: Fixed in 2cbf96e: sanitize_socket_name now appends a deterministic FNV-1a hash of the original name

title: list_and_watch never re-polls DeviceDiscovery::discover(), so health changes are never reported to kubelet
description:
core::DeviceDiscovery::discover() is documented as reporting devices' current health, implying it can be re-polled. Its only caller, DevicePluginService::list_and_watch (lib/src/lib.rs:205-228), invokes discover() a single time when the kubelet opens the stream, sends one ListAndWatchResponse, then only waits on tx.closed() to detect disconnection -- it never calls discover() again. If a device transitions Healthy -> Unhealthy while the stream is open, kubelet never learns about it and keeps scheduling/using pods on the dead device indefinitely, violating the ListAndWatch protocol contract.

This is effectively the core gap that o99.7 (Support dynamic device state and streaming updates) needs to close.

Found by high-effort code-review workflow, 2026-07-05.
close_reason: Fixed in 2cbf96e: list_and_watch now re-polls discover() on a configurable interval and pushes diffs

title: Split lib/src/lib.rs's inline test module into a separate tests.rs file
description:
## Summary

`lib/src/lib.rs` has grown to ~1150 lines, and the inline `#[cfg(test)]
mod tests { ... }` block (lines 458-1148) is more than half of that.
Split it into its own file so the production code (registration lifecycle,
`DevicePluginService` RPC handlers, socket-name sanitization) is easier to
read on its own.

## Details

- Move the body of `mod tests { ... }` (everything currently between the
  braces) into a new `lib/src/tests.rs`, unwrapped (the file's top-level
  content becomes the module body — no outer `mod tests { }` wrapper
  needed in the new file).
- In `lib/src/lib.rs`, replace the inline block with `#[cfg(test)]\nmod
  tests;` — default module-file resolution finds `lib/src/tests.rs`
  without needing a `#[path = "..."]` attribute, since the module is
  named `tests` and the file is named `tests.rs` in the same directory.
- Apply the same hoist-imports-to-parent, `use super::*;` pattern already
  used elsewhere in this codebase (see `core/src/lib.rs` and its
  submodules) if it simplifies the split, but this is secondary to the
  main goal of just moving the test code out.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `lib/src/lib.rs` no longer contains the inline test module body —
      just a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` declaration.
- [ ] `lib/src/tests.rs` contains everything the inline module had,
      unchanged in behavior.
- [ ] `cargo test -p k8s-device-plugin-lib` passes with the same test
      count as before the split.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo
      fmt --check` remain clean.
